newsitem.title: MONTSERRAT: Montserrat volcano spews ash, hot rock.
newsitem.headline: Montserrat volcano spews ash, hot rock.

text.p: Montserrat's troublesome volcano spewed ash as far as a passing cruise ship and spilled hot rock into the sea on Thursday in what scientists termed its most violent activity in months.

The early morning pyroclastic flow of hot rocks, ash and gases travelled through the Tar River valley to the sea, accompanied by an ash cloud that rose to about 20,000 feet (7,000 metres) at about dawn, according to scientists at the Montserrat Volcano Observatory.
"These events were the largest for some time," said a spokesman for the Montserrat Government Information Service.
Scientists watching the volcano had been predicting increased activity for several weeks because of mounting pressure within the rumbling Soufriere Hills volcano.
Montserrat, a small island in the eastern Caribbean, has been plagued by the volcano since it burst to life in July 1995, after a century of virtual dormancy.
The threatening mountain forced the evacuation of the island's southern end. Most of the 7,000 residents who remained on the island moved to the north, which is considered to be safe.

Scientists said a major collapse of the lava dome within the volcano could occur at any time, but noted that if a major dome collapse happened it would probably build up over the course of several hours.
They also said an explosive eruption could follow such a collapse.
